defects.description: The docstring states the sweep re-executes at HEAD; the handler resolves the casting commit instead. Drove Foundry-Phase inspect_start on a two-commit tree and the worktree checked out the older commit.

The same contract is still misdescribed one function down: the return docstring promises elapsed seconds per log and the handler reports one figure for the sweep. Drove it with two logs and read one number back.

Third consecutive cycle of the same class, now in the report module: the docstring promises a refusal naming the unreadable ledger and the handler returned a generic message. Drove it against a torn defects.json and read no filename back.

The table header for the escalated-classes section says Packets where the ledger field is structural_packets_dispatched. Reads as a shorthand rather than a claim, so no operator has been misled yet, but the same class at a finer boundary.
defects.reproduction_attempted: Read every branch of _render_section against its section's contract row and diffed the rendered headings; the boundary is finer than D-003's, at the per-row level rather than the per-refusal level, and no rendered row disagreed with its ledger. Nothing reproduced.

defects.description: The empty-table sentinel reads None recorded, which a reader could take as a measurement of zero rather than as an absent ledger. Finer boundary than D-004: one cell, not one header.
defects.reproduction_attempted: Rendered all eleven sections from three synthetic archives and compared every emitted cell against the source ledger value; the boundary is finer again, at the cell level. Zero cells disagreed. Nothing reproduced.

defects.description: Foundry-Spend is registered on the MCP surface and its handler is never reached. Drove the tool and read spend.jsonl back empty.
Filed before the tier axis existed, so it carries no tier key at all. Foundry-Next does not display the spend roll-up it is contracted to show.
